title: Local realization of a finitely presented module at a site point
statement: Let $C$ be a site small in the coefficient universe and having finite limits [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Let $R$ be a sheaf of commutative rings on $C$, let $p:\mathbf{Set}\to\operatorname{Sh}(C)$ be a point [def-trf-geometric-morphism], and set $R_p=p^{-1}R$. Let $M$ be a finitely presented $R_p$-module [def-sc-finitely-presented-module]. There exist an object $U$ of $C$, an element $x\in p^{-1}(h_U^\#)$, and a sheaf $F$ of $R_U$-modules on the localized site $C/U$ [def-pur-localized-ringed-site, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] with the following properties. Here $h_U(V)=\operatorname{Hom}_C(V,U)$ and $h_U^\#$ is its sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. The element $x$ specifies a point $q:\mathbf{Set}\to\operatorname{Sh}(C/U)$ with $j_Uq\cong p$, where $j_U^{-1}$ is restriction to $C/U$. There are canonical identifications $q^{-1}R_U\cong R_p$ and $q^{-1}(G|_U)\cong p^{-1}G$, natural in all $R$-module sheaves $G$, and an $R_p$-linear isomorphism $q^{-1}F\cong M$. The sheaf $F$ can be chosen as the cokernel of a map $R_U^a\to R_U^b$ given by a finite matrix with entries in $R(U)$, for some natural numbers $a,b$.

proof.text: Reconstruct a Mathlib GrothendieckTopology.Point with fiber sitePointFunctor J p. Coverage jointly-surjectivity extends to all covering sieves by induction on the generated topology. Mathlib Point.over supplies the localized point with a skyscraper right adjoint. The fromOverFunctorElementsEquivalence identifies its fiber diagram with the diagram on Over n. Finality gives the displayed localized section-colimit functor, hence q with exactly the prescribed inverse image.

proof.text: Normalize the original set-colimit comparison using the reconstruction theorem. Its germ formula determines the natural isomorphism. Finality of the opposite neighborhood forgetful functor gives the localized comparison. On module stalks use the corresponding finality isomorphism of additive colimits; represent a scalar and a module element at a common stage to prove linearity over the specified stalk-ring cocone. This gives the natural module comparison and both required germ formulas.

proof.text: After forgetting modules to abelian groups, the localized module stalk is naturally isomorphic to the composite of the module-to-abelian-sheaf functor and the localized point sheaf fiber. Both preserve finite colimits, and module forgetting reflects them. The additive colimit comparison for the unit sheaf is linear and identifies its stalk with the stalk ring. Transporting the coproduct universal property therefore identifies finite free sheaf stalks with free modules; evaluate the coprojections at 1 to normalize this identification on basis germs.

proof.text: Use Module.FinitePresentation.exists_fin' to choose a right-exact finite free presentation of M. Represent every matrix coefficient in the filtered colimit ring and choose a common stage using IsFiltered.sup_objs_exists. This also supplies a stage when the finite indexing set is empty. The restricted representatives give the matrix over R(U), with exactly the chosen coefficients as germs.

proof.text: Use the free-sheaf Hom equivalence and the sections given by sums of restricted coefficients times basis sections to construct alpha. Functoriality of R and the section identities prove naturality. On basis germs, linearity of colimit coprojections identifies the stalk matrix with the original presentation matrix. The localized module stalk preserves the cokernel; cokernel.mapIso and the cokernel cofork of the right-exact presentation identify its stalk with M. Choose F=cokernel alpha, retaining the exact matrix-section formula.
